newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Venture shares in tug-of-war after product launch.
newsitem.headline: Venture shares in tug-of-war after product launch.

text.p: The share price of Venture Manufacturing faced some upside resistance on Monday after surging on the announcement of its new multimedia software NovaStation.
Dealers said there were opposing forces in the market -- one trying to push the shares higher and the other taking profit.

"It seems there is one party eager to bring the price up, most likely to S$10. On the other hand there are some funds who have invested in Venture for long term growth and they are taking profit," one dealer said.
On Friday, the announcement of NovaStation sent Venture's shares rocketing to a high of S$7.10, up S$1.95.
On Monday morning, the shares surged to a high of S$8.00, but then struggled. At 0751 GMT, the shares were at S$7.10, up S$0.25. Volume was active at about 4.8 million shares.
Initial reactions from analysts and investors were that NovaStation could add as much as S$8-12 million to Venture's net profit for the financial year ending December 31, 1997.

NovaStation, developed by Venture unit Innovative Trek Technologies Pte Ltd (ITT), is a multimedia software that upgrades SoundBlaster and 16-bit compatible soundcards. It runs on Intel MMX and older 100 MHz Pentium systems.
Some analysts also thought NovaStation would compete with Creative Technology's soundcard business and Venture's announcement knocked off as much as S$2.00 off Creative's share price on Friday.
At 0751 GMT on MOnday, Creative was down another S$1.00 to S$33.50 on light volumes.
Securities house Schroders said in an investment note on Monday that Venture's share price surge was overdone.
"We think that Venture's very rapid run-up has been unjustified, given the fact that the installed base of PCs with Intel's MMX CPUs will still not be present in a large enough base," it said.
It said there were other similar solutions available like Creative's wavetable synthesizer for US$20, although they do not tap MMX technologies yet.
NovaStation is being sold through bundling with original equipment manufacturer's products and would sell on the shelves at a recomended price of US$49.
NovaStation could also face stiff competition in the next one to two years, Schroders said.

Schroders said it was looking at NovaStation adding S$3-4 million to Venture's bottom line next year. A 15-20 times price earnings ratio for Venture in 1998, with earnings projections of S$53-70 million, would bring the share price back to S$5.70-5.80, it said.
Pricing in ITT's estimated earnings for 1999 at a generous 15 times and Venture's existing operations at 15 times, would give a fair value of S$6 for the shares, Schroders said.
ING-Barings said on Monday it was looking at NovaStation achieving S$58 million in sales over a 12-month period and about S$19 million for the current fiscal year.
"Assuming a 20 percent net profit margin, that would work out to about S$10 million impact on Venture's bottom line over a 12-month period," ING-Barings said.
